The predicate is now SQL (`phone !~ PHONE_BASIC_PATTERN`, with NULL and '' still excluded), and the check takes the `leadsWithoutEmail` shape: one COUNT for the total and one `.limit(OFFENDER_LIMIT)` read for the examples, so the database does the filtering and at most ten rows come back. The pattern is not the JS regex verbatim: Postgres resolves the digit and whitespace classes through the collation, and the verbatim form disagreed with JavaScript under C, en_US.UTF-8, pg_c_utf8 and und-x-icu; the spelled-out one agrees on every code point under all four, which data-quality-leads.db.spec.ts asserts. No select in this file is flagged any more, so BOUNDED makes the gate fail if an unbounded one comes back.
